title: Routing LLM Inference in Production: From Engine Signals to Policy — Qianru Lao & Lu Zhang, OpenAI
talk_summary: OpenAI's inference load balancer evolved from a feedback-loop (P-controller) weighting scheme driven by engine signals to an explicit control-plane/data-plane architecture where a global optimizer computes routing weights offline and data planes pull snapshots locally. They also describe protection mechanisms: outlier penalties, retry budgets, and load shedding.

takeaways.what_they_do: A global control plane periodically computes routing weights from live signals plus offline capacity/latency profiles and publishes snapshots; data planes pull them asynchronously so no request waits on the control plane.
takeaways.evidence_quote: only the first pass is synchronous but it's fast and only local inside the data plane

takeaways.technique: Explicit optimizer over opaque feedback loops
takeaways.what_they_do: They replaced a self-tuning P-controller with an explicit optimization that minimizes expected end-to-end latency subject to hard constraints (serve all demand, stay within capacity, non-negative weights), because the feedback loop was hard to reason about and oscillated.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the feedback loop sometimes creates bad oscillations

takeaways.technique: End-to-end latency objective including network distance
takeaways.what_they_do: The optimizer minimizes total end-to-end latency combining network distance and engine-side queueing, so a farther engine beats a near-but-full one.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a further engine might be faster end to end

takeaways.what_they_do: Follow-up turns of the same conversation are routed back to the engine holding the KV cache to avoid recomputation and cut latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sending the follow-up turns of the same conversation back to the same engine will avoid recomputation

takeaways.what_they_do: Retries are capped by a budget that shrinks under heavy utilization to prevent retry storms, and expands when the system is healthy.

takeaways.technique: Outlier penalty and graceful load shedding
takeaways.what_they_do: Outlier engines get reduced weight to recover or be replaced; when capacity can't meet demand they proactively shed a portion of traffic to degrade gracefully instead of failing everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we basically proactively load shed a portion of the traffic to have the system degraded gracefully
